A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent partial causal model and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic identifiability experiments, CelebA reconstructions, and CLIP few-shot and domain-generalization results, including supplementary results in Appendices H–J.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds image- and text-factor recovery results on Multimodal3DIdent in Appendix P.

M1.justification: The coupled-variable generative model, symmetric contrastive objective, FastICA and PCA-plus-FastICA procedures, and Tip-Adapter integration are retained. Revised theoretical assumptions and additional explanations do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Appendix P adds Multimodal3DIdent, extending quantitative latent recovery to complex paired images and text with known generative factors. The existing synthetic, CelebA, ImageNet-family and eleven-dataset few-shot coverage remains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same linear-probe variants, Tip-Adapter, Tip-Adapter-F and their FastICA variants. Appendix P introduces no evaluated comparator; its reference to Daunhawer et al. does not constitute a new baseline comparison.

E3.justification: The new Appendix P evaluation selects object shape with seven discrete values and three position coordinates as shared factors, treats remaining factors as modality-specific, and reports recovery R2 separately for image and text. Existing shot counts, backbones, metrics and documented experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The assumption-violation experiments, ImageNet distribution-shift evaluations and CelebA traversals are retained unchanged. Appendix L adds discussion without an additional ablation, while Appendix P supplies benchmark recovery scores without a separate controlled robustness or sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repetitions for the synthetic experiments and retain their uncertainty summaries. Appendix P uses the existing plus/minus reporting style without documenting a new run-count, seed, confidence-interval or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix P and Figure 9 newly report Multimodal3DIdent recovery R2 of 0.97 ± 0.05 for images and 0.75 ± 0.04 for text. These are additional results under new conditions; matched synthetic and ImageNet-family table values, CelebA images and few-shot curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 revise the stated mixing-map assumptions from nonlinear/invertible to invertible/differentiable. Appendix C adds explicit KDE convergence conditions, and Appendix D.1 adds an argument for uniqueness up to isometries and permutations. Appendix O formalizes disentanglement, while the principal identifiability conclusions and most derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a non-DAG coupled-variable model, linear/permutation identifiability, component-wise disentanglement potential, and practical CLIP benefits. Heterogeneous causal mechanisms receive greater prominence in v3, but v2 already used conflicting DAG structures to motivate the same contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 and Appendix N explicitly discuss unverifiable real-world generative assumptions and downstream performance as surrogate evidence. Appendix L discusses uncertainty in choosing FastICA versus PCA-plus-FastICA, and Appendix P attributes weaker text recovery to discrete factors conflicting with continuous assumptions. These qualify and extend the existing interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and a reproducibility statement promising code and instructions after publication. Appendix K retains the existing hardware, architectures and hyperparameters. Actual code availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 updates the supporting literature with multimodal foundation-model surveys, opposing data-generation examples, density-estimation and facial-hypersphere references, and expands the causal-representation discussion in Appendix A. Several classical causal-discovery references disappear, but the principal distinctions from earlier multimodal identifiability work in Appendices F–G remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around heterogeneous multimodal data generation. Section 2 presents the competing DAG mechanisms before introducing the proposed model, reversing the earlier narrative order. Contribution bullets, terminology, headings and citation style are extensively revised, with MMCL shorthand used throughout.

P2.justification: v3 adopts conference typography and page layout throughout, redraws and reverses the order of the causal diagrams, and consolidates the simulation-table captions. The small results display labeled Figure 4 in v2 becomes full-width Table 2. Appendix displays are rearranged, and a new sample-and-score Figure 9 is added; retained empirical images and curves are reused.

improvement.justification: Appendix P adds direct quantitative latent recovery on complex paired images and text, complementing v2's vector simulations, qualitative traversals and downstream evaluations. More explicit limitations and clearer diagrams and tables also help. The improvement is limited because the new experiment provides little model, training, split or uncertainty-procedure detail, constraining reproducibility and the strength of its supporting evidence.
